newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto to discuss islands dispute with Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Suharto to discuss islands dispute with Malaysia.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto is due to go to Malaysia to try to resolve a dispute over a group of islands claimed by both countries, the official Antara news agency said on Sunday.
It quoted Indonesian Army Chief-of-Staff General Feisal Tanjung as saying that Indonesia hoped the dispute over the Sipadan and Ligitan islands off the coast of Borneo could be settled amicably.

Hamid did not say when Suharto would visit Malaysia, which is also involved in a dispute over the South China Sea's Spratly Islands with Vietnam, the Philippines, Brunei, China and Taiwan.
Malaysia wants to take the Sipadan and Ligitan issue for International Court arbitration in The Hague if necessary but Hamid said Indonesia preferred a solution in the "spirit of ASEAN".
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei, Vietnam, Philippines, Thailand and Singapore.
There have been years of negotiations to find a bilateral solution to the dispute which resurfaced in 1991 when Malaysia began promoting the islands as a tourist destination.
